Section 2(a)(2)(B) states that a taxpayer shall not be considered a surviving spouse unless a joint return could have been made in the taxable year during which the spouse died, and that no joint return shall be made if either spouse is a nonresident alien at any time during the taxable year. Since Alice was a nonresident alien since March 4th, 1990 (including all of 2014 when she died), Bob cannot make a joint return for 2014, so Section 2(a)(2)(B) applies to Bob and prevents him from qualifying as a surviving spouse.
reasoning:
Let me analyze the facts and the statute carefully.

**Facts:**
- Alice and Bob got married on Feb 3rd, 1992
- Alice died on July 9th, 2014
- Alice was a nonresident alien since March 4th, 1990

**Question:** Section 2(a)(2)(B) applies to Bob in 2014.

**Statute - Section 2(a)(2)(B):**
"Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of section 1 a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a surviving spouse-
(B) unless, for the taxpayer's taxable year during which his spouse died, a joint return could have been made. A husband and wife may make a single return jointly of income taxes, even though one of the spouses has neither gross income nor deductions, except that no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien."

**Analysis:**

Section 2(a)(2)(B) is a limitation on who can be considered a surviving spouse. It states that a taxpayer shall NOT be considered a surviving spouse UNLESS a joint return could have been made in the taxable year during which the spouse died.

The statute then says: "no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien."

**Key Facts:**
- Alice died July 9th, 2014
- Alice was a nonresident alien since March 4th, 1990
- For the taxable year 2014 (when Alice died), Alice was a nonresident alien

Since Alice was a nonresident alien at any time during the taxable year 2014, a joint return could NOT have been made in 2014.

Therefore, under Section 2(a)(2)(B), Bob shall NOT be considered a surviving spouse.

The question asks: "Section 2(a)(2)(B) applies to Bob in 2014."

Section 2(a)(2)(B) IS the rule that determines whether someone can be considered a surviving spouse. 

The limitation in 2(a)(2)(B) is indeed what governs Bob's eligibility. Since Alice was a nonresident alien in 2014, the condition that would allow Bob to qualify as a surviving spouse cannot be met—this limitation clause directly applies to prevent him from being considered a surviving spouse under the statute.

The question hinges on whether "applies" means the provision governs the analysis or whether it permits surviving spouse status. Since Section 2(a)(2)(B) is the operative restriction preventing the status from being granted, it does apply to Bob in 2014.
